spec: FR-2.15, 03 §4, task 004 stage 7. Every record standing after a history passed oldest first, with the session and set that set it — what the server's personal_records cache stores. The fold is personal_bests', so the values always match it; this file is about *where*. A later tie is not a record, so the earliest session to reach a value keeps it. A session total belongs to no one set.
expectation_shape: `expected` lists the standing records in detect_prs' order: max_weight, best_e1rm, max_reps_at_weight (lightest load first), best_session_volume. Each gives its kind, `session_index` and `set_index` (a position within that session; null for a session total), and `weight_kg` where it tells two reps records apart. `value` is written only where it is an exact sum or product; the e1RM case is fixed by its set, from which each consumer computes Epley itself.

cases.name: each record points at the session and set that set it, a warm-up taking a position and nothing else
cases.note: Session two's volume is 330 kg; its 110 x 3 has no RIR, so the e1RM stays with session one.

cases.name: a later tie leaves every record with whoever got there first
a record beaten later moves to the session that beat it, and one reps record stands per load
cases.note: No set has a RIR, so there is no e1RM record. Session one is 1400 kg and session two 1520 kg.
